correctness.rationale: From \(3\sigma(m)=4m+d\), parity gives odd \(d\) exactly when odd \(m\) is a square. Otherwise \(d\mid2m\) gives \(v_2(d)=1\), hence \(v_2(\sigma(m))=1\). Multiplicativity leaves exactly one odd prime exponent, and the exact lifting formula \(v_2(\sigma(p^a))=v_2(p+1)+v_2(a+1)-1\) forces \(p\equiv a\equiv1\pmod4\). The actual finite verifier was inspected but is only corroborative.

final_claim: If a near-perfect integer satisfies \(v_2(n)=1\), write \(n=2m\) with \(m\) odd. Then either \(m\) is a square and the redundant divisor is odd, or \(m=p^{4u+1}s^2\) with \(p\equiv1\pmod4\), \(p\nmid s\), and the redundant divisor is \(2\pmod4\); the redundant divisor is odd exactly in the square branch.
